title: Can a pathological liar be cured? with Drew Curtis, PhD, and Christian L. Hart, PhD

sentences.en: Almost everyone lies occasionally.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有人都偶尔说谎。

sentences.en: Even if you consider yourself scrupulously honest, you've probably told the occasional fib.
sentences.zh: 即使你认为自己绝对诚实，你也可能偶尔说过善意的谎言。

sentences.en: But for a small percentage of people, lying isn't something that they do every once in a while.
sentences.zh: 但对极少数人来说，说谎并非偶尔为之。

sentences.en: It's a way of life.
sentences.zh: 而是一种生活方式。

sentences.en: Researchers have found that while most people tell between zero and two lies per day on average, the most prolific liars might tell five, ten, or even twenty.
sentences.zh: 研究发现，虽然大多数人平均每天说零到两个谎，但最习惯说谎的人可能会说五个、十个甚至二十个。

sentences.en: In recent weeks, the liar most in the news has been newly elected Representative George Santos,
sentences.zh: 在最近几周里，最受关注的骗子是新当选的众议员乔治·桑托斯，

sentences.en: whose long list of career embellishments, deceptions, and outright falsehoods came to light only after he won his seat.
sentences.zh: 他那长长的一串职业镀金、欺骗和彻头彻尾的谎言，直到他赢得席位后才曝光。

sentences.en: Santos appears to have made up college degrees, real estate holdings, even Jewish ancestry, among his many other fabrications.
sentences.zh: 桑托斯除了许多其他的捏造之外，似乎还虚构了大学学位、房地产持有量，甚至犹太血统。

sentences.en: So what drives big liars to lie?
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么驱使大说谎家们说谎呢？

sentences.en: And are their motivations different from those other people who lie less frequently?
sentences.zh: 他们的动机与那些说谎频率较低的人有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: Is pathological lying a mental health disorder?
sentences.zh: 病理性说谎是一种心理健康障碍吗？

sentences.en: How common is it?
sentences.zh: 这种情况有多普遍？

sentences.en: And are liars more prevalent in some professions, like politics or sales, or are those unfounded stereotypes?
sentences.zh: 在政界或销售等某些职业中，骗子是不是更常见，还是这只是一种毫无根据的刻板印象？

sentences.en: Are there differences in lying between men and women, people of different social backgrounds, or among people who consider themselves religious?
sentences.zh: 男性和女性、不同社会背景的人，或者自认为有宗教信仰的人，在说谎方面有什么区别吗？

sentences.en: And finally, how can you recognize prolific liars in your life and protect yourself from being duped?
sentences.zh: 最后，你如何在生活中识别出习惯性说谎者并保护自己免受欺骗？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学说话》，这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客，探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: We have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 我们今天请到了两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: The first is Dr. Drew Curtis, an Associate Professor of Psychology and Director of the Master's and Doctoral Programs in Counseling Psychology
sentences.zh: 第一位是德鲁·柯蒂斯博士，他是心理学副教授兼咨询心理学硕士和博士项目主任，

sentences.en: at Angelo State University in San Angelo, Texas.
sentences.zh: 位于德克萨斯州圣安杰洛的安杰洛州立大学。

sentences.en: Dr. Curtis is a licensed clinical psychologist who studies pathological lying and deception, particularly in the context of therapy and within healthcare professions,
sentences.zh: 柯蒂斯博士是一名执业临床心理学家，专门研究病理性说谎和欺骗，特别是在治疗、医疗保健职业、

sentences.en: intimate relationships, and parental relationships.
sentences.zh: 亲密关系和父母关系中。

sentences.en: Our second guest is Dr. Christian Hart, a Professor of Psychology and Director of the Psychological Science Graduate Program at Texas Women's University.
sentences.zh: 我们的第二位嘉宾是克里斯蒂安·哈特博士，他是德克萨斯女子大学的心理学教授兼心理科学研究生项目主任。

sentences.en: He is an experimental psychologist who conducts research primarily on lying and deception.
sentences.zh: 他是一名实验心理学家，主要从事说谎和欺骗方面的研究。

sentences.en: He is also the former president and current executive director of the Southwestern Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 他也是西南心理学协会的前任会长和现任执行董事。

sentences.en: Drs.
sentences.zh: 柯蒂斯博士

sentences.en: Curtis and Hart are the co-authors of the book
sentences.zh: 和哈特博士是该书的共同作者，

sentences.en: Pathological Lying, Theory, Research, and Practice, which was published in November by APA Books.
sentences.zh: 书名为《病理性说谎：理论、研究与实践》，该书于11月由APA出版社出版。

sentences.en: They are also writing a book for the general public called
sentences.zh: 他们还在为大众写一本书，书名为

sentences.en: Big Liars, What Psychological Science Tells Us About Lying and How You Can Avoid Being Duped, which will be published by APA Books later this year.
sentences.zh: 《大说谎家：心理科学告诉我们关于谎言的真相以及你如何避免被骗》，该书将于今年晚些时候由APA出版社出版。

sentences.en: Thank you both for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢两位今天做客。

sentences.en: It's a great pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 非常高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thanks for having us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我们。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: Well, I started the introduction talking about how we all lie sometimes.
sentences.zh: 好的，我在开场白里谈到了我们有时都会说谎。

sentences.en: So what is the difference between someone who just lies occasionally and a pathological liar?
sentences.zh: 那么，偶尔说谎的人和病理性说谎者之间有什么区别？

sentences.en: Is it just how often they're lying or are the causes and motivations different?
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是因为他们说谎的频率，还是原因和动机有所不同？

sentences.en: Dr. Curtis, you want to take that one?
sentences.zh: 柯蒂斯博士，你想回答这个问题吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: A lot of our work has really set out to ask that question among people who lie.
sentences.zh: 我们的大量工作确实旨在向说谎的人群提出这个问题。

sentences.en: Is there a clinical population?
sentences.zh: 是否存在一个临床群体？

sentences.en: Is there a group that's different from people who might tell big liars?
sentences.zh: 是否存在一个不同于那些可能会说弥天大谎的人的群体？

sentences.en: And essentially, we found and put forth theory and research that suggests there is.
sentences.zh: 本质上，我们发现并提出了理论和研究，表明确实存在。

sentences.en: And so the criteria for pathological lying is people who tell an excessive amount of lies,
sentences.zh: 因此，病理性说谎的标准是那些说谎成性的人，

sentences.en: and that impairs their functioning, brings about distress, and poses some kind of risk of danger to themselves or others.
sentences.zh: 这损害了他们的功能，带来了痛苦，并对他们自己或他人构成了某种危险。

sentences.en: Dr. Hart, let me ask you, what about the substance of the lies?
sentences.zh: 哈特博士，请问谎言的实质是什么？

sentences.en: When we're talking about a pathological liar, does that person tell different lies from just, you know, your average everyday garden variety liar?
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论病理性说谎者时，这个人说谎的内容与你我身边的普通日常说谎者不同吗？

sentences.en: Well, there's not a lot of research on that topic.
sentences.zh: 关于这个话题的研究并不多。

sentences.en: What we can gather from reading through the extensive case literature on pathological liars over the past century is that their lies tend to be somewhat varied.
sentences.zh: 从过去一个世纪对病理性说谎者的大量案例文献中，我们可以推断出他们的谎言往往有些多样化。

sentences.en: We can find some pretty clear cases where they're lying for some sort of financial motivation or financial gain.
sentences.zh: 我们可以发现一些非常明显的案例，他们为了某种财务动机或经济利益而说谎。

sentences.en: But one of the patterns that we tend to see perhaps more than you'd see in your typical everyday form of liar is lies that are aimed at bringing attention on oneself.
sentences.zh: 但我们倾向于看到的一种模式——也许比你在典型日常形式的说谎者中看到的更多——是为了引起他人注意的谎言。

sentences.en: And so that's probably the biggest distinction that we see.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是我们看到的最大区别。

sentences.en: Pathological lying is not, at the moment, considered a mental health diagnosis,
sentences.zh: 病理性说谎目前不被视为心理健康诊断，

sentences.en: but you have both advocated for it to be added to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders.
sentences.zh: 但你们俩都主张将其加入《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》中。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Why do you want to see that?
sentences.zh: 你为什么希望看到这一点？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's got a robust history in clinical psychiatry and psychology.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为它在临床精神病学和心理学中有着深厚的发展历史。

sentences.en: A lot of our work and research on the literature, the most prominent psychiatrists, the times, you know, late 1800s, early 1900s,
sentences.zh: 我们对文献的大量工作和研究表明，当时最著名的精神病学家，你知道的，19世纪末、20世纪初，

sentences.en: have well-documented the existence of pathological lying.
sentences.zh: 已经充分记录了病理性说谎的存在。

sentences.en: And it's held different names, you know, like Pseudologia Fantastica, Mythomania.
sentences.zh: 它有不同的名称，比如虚构症、狂言症。

sentences.en: And so it's been well-documented and tucked away by what we would say is the most prolific, prominent researchers and clinicians throughout time.
sentences.zh: 因此，它已被我们所说的历代最高产、最杰出的研究人员和临床医生很好地记录并保存下来。

sentences.en: And so it's been recognized by them early on.
sentences.zh: 所以它很早就被他们认可了。

sentences.en: And then some zeitgeist, essentially, we've lost it throughout time.
sentences.zh: 然后由于某种时代精神，我们随着时间的推移失去了它。

sentences.en: And so Chris and I have picked back up the gauntlet to look at this phenomena.
sentences.zh: 所以克里斯和我重新挑起重担来研究这个现象。

sentences.en: Our research has corroborated, based on that theory, that there is a group of people who their lying impairs their problems,
sentences.zh: 我们的研究基于该理论证实了确实存在这样一群人，他们的说谎损害了他们的问题，

sentences.en: and they're looking for some kind of treatment or some kind of help.
sentences.zh: 并且他们在寻求某种治疗或某种帮助。

sentences.en: So we've essentially just been very passionate to look at that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们基本上只是对研究这个非常充满热情。

sentences.en: And our research has corroborated that it should be recognized as a diagnostic entity.
sentences.zh: 我们的研究已经证实，它应该被确认为一个诊断实体。

sentences.en: How optimistic are you that you will succeed in getting the diagnosis included?
sentences.zh: 你对成功将这一诊断纳入有多大信心？

sentences.en: And what's involved in that?
sentences.zh: 这其中涉及什么？

sentences.en: There's a lot involved.
sentences.zh: 这里面涉及很多东西。

sentences.en: And I guess I'm fairly optimistic.
sentences.zh: 我想我还是相当乐观的。

sentences.en: You know, the DSM, the American Psychiatric Association, has criteria for what needs to be done when submitting that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，DSM，即美国精神病学协会，对于提交申请时需要完成的事情有相应的标准。

sentences.en: And there's a task force and many intelligent people working hard to recognize these things.
sentences.zh: 有一个工作组和许多聪明人在努力工作以认可这些事情。

sentences.en: It's not maybe what some of the common public thinks, is you just create a label to stigmatize people, that it's a pretty lengthy process.
sentences.zh: 这可能不像一些普通公众认为的那样，仅仅是创造一个标签来污名化人们，这是一个相当漫长的过程。

sentences.en: And you have to show that there's the existence of something that people struggle with.
sentences.zh: 你必须证明人们正在与之抗争的某种东西的存在。

sentences.en: And by providing a label, there's going to do more benefit than cause harm.
sentences.zh: 并且通过提供一个标签，带来的好处将大于造成的伤害。

sentences.en: And so I think not only our work, but work of others before us have demonstrated that there's more people who truly suffer from this and want help.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为不仅我们的工作，还有在我们之前其他人的工作都表明，有更多的人真正因此痛苦并需要帮助。

sentences.en: Anecdotally, we've had people reach out to us via email saying, hey, I came across your work and I'm willing to travel across several states for treatment.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，曾有人通过电子邮件联系我们，说，嘿，我看到了你们的工作，我愿意跨越好几个州来接受治疗。

sentences.en: I need help with this.
sentences.zh: 我需要这方面的帮助。

sentences.en: Or a significant other, marriage is about to end and desperately need some help.
sentences.zh: 或者某个另一半，婚姻即将破裂，极其需要一些帮助。

sentences.en: And can you help me?
sentences.zh: 你们能帮帮我吗？

sentences.en: And it's unfortunate when we don't label it as a diagnostic entity.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不把它贴上诊断实体的标签，那就太不幸了。

sentences.en: You know, at this point, we can't say we can formally call it anything and can't treat you accordingly.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在这一点上，我们不能说我们可以正式称它为什么，也不能相应地治疗你。

sentences.en: And so it would be beneficial then to the person who thinks that they have the disorder, that their insurance, for example, would cover the treatment.
sentences.zh: 因此，这对认为自己患有这种疾病的人是有益的，例如他们的保险可以报销治疗费用。

sentences.en: And that's why we need this, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们需要这个，对吧？

sentences.en: That's one of the major reasons.
sentences.zh: 这是主要原因之一。

sentences.en: You certainly want some insurance to cover treatment.
sentences.zh: 你当然希望某种保险能涵盖治疗费用。

sentences.en: And then another reason we want to recognize treatment is so researchers can start looking at what are the effective treatments?
sentences.zh: 我们希望认可治疗的另一个原因是，研究人员可以开始研究什么是有效的治疗方法？

sentences.en: What are the empirically supported treatments that we can use to help people treat this in the most cost-effective and time-effective manner?
sentences.zh: 有哪些我们可以用来以最具成本效益和时间效益的方式帮助人们治疗这一问题的经验支持的疗法？

sentences.en: Dr. Hart, let me ask you, how common is pathological lying?
sentences.zh: 哈特博士，请问病理性说谎有多普遍？

sentences.en: Do we know what percentage of the population might qualify as a pathological liar?
sentences.zh: 我们知道人口中有多少比例的人可能有资格被称为病理性说谎者吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, answering that question has been a little problematic.
sentences.zh: 是的，回答这个问题有点问题。

sentences.en: Historically, researchers have looked at it, but they've looked at it within kind of narrow populations,
sentences.zh: 历史上，研究人员对此进行了研究，但他们是在相当狭窄的人群中进行研究的，

sentences.en: populations that were having, you know, people in juvenile detention facilities and things like that,
sentences.zh: 比如那些在少年管教所等地方的人群，

sentences.en: where obviously you might expect the rates to be considerably higher than the general population.
sentences.zh: 很显然，你可能会预料到那里的比例会大大高于普通人口。

sentences.en: And Drew and I conducted a study that we published a few years ago where we tried to look at this.
sentences.zh: 德鲁和我进行了一项研究，我们在几年前发表了这项研究，我们试图探讨这个问题。

sentences.en: And based on the data we collected, we are showing rates around like 8% to 13%.
sentences.zh: 根据我们收集的数据，我们显示比例大约在8%到13%左右。

sentences.en: But a big caveat with that is we are collecting data from people on websites
sentences.zh: 但其中一个很大的注意事项是，我们是从网站上的人群中收集数据的，

sentences.en: where they might have some particular interest in this and might be more likely to have a problem with lying.
sentences.zh: 他们在该问题上可能有某种特殊的兴趣，并且更有可能存在说谎问题。

sentences.en: So, the more recent data that we've collected that we talk about in our book, I think we would put the rate at somewhere closer to 5%, if not even smaller than that.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们在书中讨论的最近收集的数据表明，我认为比例应该更接近5%，甚至比那还要小。

sentences.en: And one other thing there, you know, without having this as a diagnostic entity labeled,
sentences.zh: 还有一点，你知道的，如果没有将其作为贴上标签的诊断实体，

sentences.en: we can't collect some of that data too.
sentences.zh: 我们也无法收集其中一些数据。

sentences.en: So, I think it's, you know, chicken or egg.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这就像是先有鸡还是先有蛋的问题。

sentences.en: Once we recognize pathological lying in the DSM, then as it's getting diagnosed, we can get more accurate data of what its prevalence is.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们在DSM中承认了病理性说谎，随着它的被诊断，我们就能获得关于其流行率的更准确的数据。

sentences.en: Now, your book talks about differences in lying based on gender, social status, and some other demographic characteristics.
sentences.zh: 现在，你们的书讨论了根据性别、社会地位和其他一些人口统计学特征在说谎方面的差异。

sentences.en: Could you detail what you and other researchers have found in those areas?
sentences.zh: 你能详细说明你和其他研究人员在这些领域发现了什么吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I'll talk a little bit about that.
sentences.zh: 我会稍微谈谈这一点。

sentences.en: With gender, we don't really see any gender differences in the frequency with which people lie.
sentences.zh: 在性别方面，我们在人们说谎的频率上没有看到任何性别差异。

sentences.en: We do see some differences in the types of things that men and women lie about.
sentences.zh: 我们在男女说谎的事情类型上确实看到了一些差异。

sentences.en: For instance, women are more apt to tell lies that are relational in nature,
sentences.zh: 例如，女性更有可能说本质上具有关系性质的谎言，

sentences.en: whereas men are more apt to tell more kind of self-serving, selfish lies.
sentences.zh: 而男性则更有可能说更偏向自我服务、自私的谎言。

sentences.en: I guess it would be the best way to describe them.
sentences.zh: 我想这是描述它们的最好方式。

sentences.en: We see some other traits and characteristics that are associated with more frequent lying.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了与更频繁说谎相关的其他一些特质和特征。

sentences.en: You know, you mentioned religiosity at the beginning of this program.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你在节目开始时提到了宗教信仰。

sentences.en: We actually just completed a fairly large study on that topic and didn't find much of a relationship at all between religiosity and lying.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上刚刚就这个话题完成了一项相当大的研究，并没有发现宗教信仰与说谎之间有太大的关系。

sentences.en: Age is probably the biggest factor.
sentences.zh: 年龄可能是最大的因素。

sentences.en: If we look at the frequency of lying across the time, across the lifespan, lying seems to peak in late adolescence.
sentences.zh: 如果我们纵观一生中说谎的频率，说谎似乎在青春期后期达到顶峰。

sentences.en: So it kind of gradually increases throughout childhood, peaks in late adolescence, and then slowly declines across adulthood.
sentences.zh: 所以它在整个童年时期逐渐增加，在青春期后期达到顶峰，然后在成年期缓慢下降。

sentences.en: So age is certainly the factor that we've identified so far that seems to be the strongest predictor of lying.
sentences.zh: 因此，年龄无疑是我们迄今为止确定的似乎是说谎最强预测指标的因素。

sentences.en: Then we also have personality traits.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还有人格特质。

sentences.en: So your listeners are probably familiar with the dark triad personality traits, all these different malevolent personality traits.
sentences.zh: 所以你的听众可能熟悉暗黑三合型人格特质，所有这些不同的恶劣人格特质。

sentences.en: Those tend to be associated with lying.
sentences.zh: 这些往往与说谎有关。

sentences.en: Looking at kind of big five personality traits, we find that people who are low in agreeableness and high in neuroticism are more likely to lie.
sentences.zh: 从大五人格特质来看，我们发现宜人性低和神经质高的人更有可能说谎。

sentences.en: And then finally, people who have low self-esteem are much more inclined to lie than those who have higher levels of self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 最后，自卑的人比自尊心更强的人更有倾向说谎。

sentences.en: So I think the research shows that lying in people starts around age three, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我想研究表明，人们从三岁左右开始说谎，对吧？

sentences.en: That's when children first figure out that they can sort of fib to mom and dad.
sentences.zh: 那是孩子们第一次发现他们可以对爸爸妈妈撒谎的时候。

sentences.en: But at what age does pathological lying start?
sentences.zh: 但是病理性说谎从什么年龄开始呢？

sentences.en: Do you know?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: Our work has largely suggested the onset primarily in adolescence, late childhood adolescence.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作在很大程度上表明发病主要在青春期，晚期儿童青春期。

sentences.en: And so one of the studies that Chris and I with Dr. Victoria Tau are currently working on is looking at an adolescent sample to look at some more specific factors of etiology.
sentences.zh: 因此，克里斯和我与维多利亚·陶博士目前正在进行的一项研究是观察青少年样本，以寻找病因的一些更具体的因素。

sentences.en: So looking at executive functioning within that group and looking at the onset.
sentences.zh: 因此，研究该群体内的执行功能并观察发病情况。

sentences.en: So digging a little deeper into adolescence.
sentences.zh: 所以对青春期进行更深入的研究。

sentences.en: There is a stereotype of dishonest politicians with George Santos being a very extreme example right now, although not the only one, or other types of snake oil salesmen.
sentences.zh: 存在一种不诚实政客的刻板印象，乔治·桑托斯目前就是一个非常极端的例子，尽管不是唯一的例子，或者是其他类型的江湖骗子。

sentences.en: Is there a kernel of truth to that?
sentences.zh: 这其中有核心的真相吗？

sentences.en: Are pathological liars more common in some professions than others?
sentences.zh: 病理性说谎者在某些职业中比其他职业更常见吗？

sentences.en: We haven't seen any evidence of that.
sentences.zh: 我们没有看到这方面的任何证据。

sentences.en: When we look at lying generally, we see that people tend to lie when they have a motivation or an incentive to lie.
sentences.zh: 当我们普遍看待说谎时，我们发现当人们有说谎的动机或诱因时，他们倾向于说谎。

sentences.en: And those motivations and incentives are more common in some professions than others, certainly.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些动机和诱因在某些职业中比其他职业更常见。

sentences.en: In sales and in politics, it's very difficult to be entirely honest and effectively do one's job.
sentences.zh: 在销售和政治领域，要做到完全诚实并有效地完成工作是非常困难的。

sentences.en: And so taking politics as an example, we can see that people who go into politics don't seem to be any less honest, typically, than people in the general population.
sentences.zh: 因此，以政治为例，我们可以看出，从事政治的人通常似乎并不比一般人群中的人更不诚实。

sentences.en: However, what we see is that politicians who lie more are much more likely to be reelected.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们看到的是，说谎更多的政客更有可能再次当选。

sentences.en: And so what it suggests is that the people who go into politics are probably no less honest
sentences.zh: 所以这表明投身政治的人可能并不比你我更不诚实，

sentences.en: than you and me, but there's something about the profession that pushes them in a direction
sentences.zh: 但这个职业的某些方面将他们推向了一个方向，

sentences.en: where they might have to conceal certain truths that might cause them to lose some of their favorability with the public and might push them to fabricate information and exaggerate
sentences.zh: 在那里他们可能不得不隐藏某些真相，这些真相可能会导致他们失去公众的一些好感，并可能促使他们捏造信息和夸大其词，

sentences.en: and perhaps even conceal the truth and lie.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能掩盖真相并说谎。

sentences.en: Well, are pathological liars aware that they are lying or do they tend to believe what they're saying?
sentences.zh: 那么，病理性说谎者是否意识到他们在说谎，还是他们往往相信自己所说的话？

sentences.en: And do they really grasp the consequences of their falsehoods?
sentences.zh: 他们真的能理解他们谎言的后果吗？

sentences.en: Our research has indicated in different research asking about questions of awareness or even
sentences.zh: 我们的研究表明，在询问有关意识或甚至是

sentences.en: some assessment research we've done where we've brought people in conducting psychological evaluations one-on-one.
sentences.zh: 我们做过的一些评估研究中，我们曾把人们带进来进行一对一的心理评估。

sentences.en: Uh, you know, many for the definition, let me back up the definition of, of being, of lying is an intentional act.
sentences.zh: 呃，你知道的，很多关于定义的说法——让我倒回来说说定义——所谓说谎，是一种故意的行为。

sentences.en: So you're, you're intentionally trying to make someone believe something you don't believe to be true.
sentences.zh: 所以你是在，你是在故意让别人相信一件你认为并非真实的事情。

sentences.en: And that definition is important for us because it helps distinguish delusion or aspects of
sentences.zh: 这个定义对我们很重要，因为它有助于区分妄想，或者

sentences.en: psychopathology of psychosis where someone's delusional, where they're actually intending to lie.
sentences.zh: 精神病学中那些人有妄想、实际上打算说谎的精神病发作的表现。

sentences.en: And so with that awareness, you know, many pathological liars are aware and they are intentionally lying.
sentences.zh: 因此，带着这种意识，你知道，许多病理性说谎者是有意识的，而且他们是故意在说谎。

sentences.en: Now, sometimes, you know, sometimes they may say it's for an innocuous reason, or sometimes they may say, um, I don't know why I said what I said.
sentences.zh: 现在，有时，你知道，有时他们可能会说这是一个无害的理由，或者有时他们可能会说，嗯，我不知道我为什么会说那样的话。

sentences.en: Or, uh, you know, someone asks you, what's your favorite cereal?
sentences.zh: 或者，呃，你知道的，有人问你，你最喜欢的麦片是什么？

sentences.en: And you say Wheaties, even though it's Cheerios.
sentences.zh: 然后你说惠氏（Wheaties），尽管其实是喜诗（Cheerios）。

sentences.en: And you're like, well, why'd you lie about that?
sentences.zh: 然后你会想，好吧，你为什么要为这事撒谎？

sentences.en: That's seemingly innocuous.
sentences.zh: 这看起来似乎是无害的。

sentences.en: Why would you do that?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: Uh, they may say something like, I'm not sure why I did.
sentences.zh: 呃，他们可能会说类似这样的话：我不太确定我为什么要这么做。

sentences.en: Uh, and then it, you know, it can build up from that, you know, becoming this, uh, monstrous lies to cover lies to cover lies.
sentences.zh: 呃，然后，你知道的，这可能会在此基础上积聚，你知道的，变成这种，呃，用谎言去掩盖谎言再掩盖谎言的滔天大谎。

sentences.en: Um, but many of the times that they are aware and in the moment they'll say doing so almost as a compulsion reduces the anxiety and they feel momentarily relief.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但很多时候他们是有意识的，并且在当下他们会说，这样做几乎就像是一种强迫症，能够减轻焦虑，并让他们获得短暂的解脱。

sentences.en: But then sometime afterwards, you know, maybe hours, maybe the next day or two, that's where
sentences.zh: 但随后在之后的某个时间，你知道的，也许是几个小时后，也许是一两天后，那就是

sentences.en: the remorse and the guilt comes in where they, they're thinking, why did I lie about Wheaties?
sentences.zh: 懊悔和内疚袭来的时刻，他们会想，我为什么要为惠氏麦片撒谎？

sentences.en: Why didn't I just say, I like Cheerios?
sentences.zh: 我为什么不直接说，我喜欢喜诗麦片？

sentences.en: Or why did I lie about my favorite band or song?
sentences.zh: 或者我为什么要谎报我最喜欢的乐队或歌曲？

sentences.en: Why did I do that?
sentences.zh: 我为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: And that's where the guilt and remorse will be present.
sentences.zh: 这就是内疚和懊悔出现的时候。

sentences.en: Are pathological liars more likely to be dishonest in other ways?
sentences.zh: 病理性说谎者是否更有可能在其他方面也不诚实？

sentences.en: For example, were they more likely to cheat on their taxes or have extramarital affairs?
sentences.zh: 例如，他们是否更有可能在纳税上欺诈或有婚外情？

sentences.en: Or is lying its own thing and it's just a separate type of dishonesty?
sentences.zh: 还是说谎本身就是一回事，它只是一种独立的不诚实行为？

sentences.en: That's another area where, uh, there's not much research, uh, that's been carried out specific on, on pathological liars that would allow us to answer that question.
sentences.zh: 这是另一个领域，呃，目前还没有针对病理性说谎者开展多少专门研究，能让我们回答这个问题。

sentences.en: However, if we look at lying more broadly, uh, what we have found in our research is that
sentences.zh: 然而，如果我们把说谎的范围放大来看，呃，我们在研究中发现的是，

sentences.en: if people tend to tell one type of lie or behave dishonest, dishonestly in one type of way, they tend to lie and be dishonest in other ways as well.
sentences.zh: 如果人们倾向于说某种类型的谎言，或者在某一方面表现得不诚实，他们也往往会在其他方面说谎和不诚实。

sentences.en: And so, for example, we've measured various categories of lies from benevolent white lies to malicious lies to kind of vindictive lies.
sentences.zh: 因此，举个例子，我们衡量了各种类别的谎言，从善意的白色谎言到恶意的谎言，再到带有一种报复性质的谎言。

sentences.en: And what we, what we find is that people who tell a lot of one type of lie tend to tell a lot of the other types of lies as well.
sentences.zh: 而我们，我们发现的是，习惯说某种谎言的人往往也会说很多其他类型的谎言。

sentences.en: So there's these strong correlations between the different types of dishonesty.
sentences.zh: 因此，不同类型的不诚实行为之间存在着这些强烈的相关性。

sentences.en: So what this suggests to us is that for the most part, if, um, if we're categorizing someone as being a prolific liar, they're probably going to be lying across domains.
sentences.zh: 所以这向我们表明，在大多数情况下，如果，嗯，如果我们把某人归类为多产的说谎者，他们很可能会在各个领域都撒谎。

sentences.en: However, we also make a point in our upcoming book that some people are deceptive in specific niche areas.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们在即将出版的书里也指出，有些人是在特定的细分领域具有欺骗性。

sentences.en: And so we're talking about occupations a little bit ago.
sentences.zh: 我们刚才也聊到过职业问题。

sentences.en: So someone might be in a position where they find themselves recurrently lying at the workplace,
sentences.zh: 所以某人可能会处于这样一个岗位：他们发现自己在工作场所经常说谎，

sentences.en: either to deal with a problematic boss or to, to, you know, sell products to customers or what have you, but then might be fairly honest with their family.
sentences.zh: 要么是为了应付问题多多的老板，要么是为了向客户推销产品，诸如此类，但对待家人时可能相当诚实。

sentences.en: And so we can have certainly examples of people who have these niche areas where they're prolific
sentences.zh: 因此，我们当然可以找到这样的人的例子：他们在这些细分领域是惯于说谎的人，

sentences.en: liars and honest and other areas, but by and large, dishonest people tend to be dishonest across the different domains of their lives.
sentences.zh: 而在其他领域则很诚实，但大体上，不诚实的人往往在他们生活的各个领域都不诚实。

sentences.en: There's a documentary that just launched on Netflix about Bernie Madoff, you know, who pulled
sentences.zh: Netflix 上刚上映了一部关于伯尼·麦道夫（Bernie Madoff）的纪录片，你知道的，他策划了

sentences.en: off the biggest investment Ponzi scheme that we have ever seen, even bigger than the similar
sentences.zh: 我们见过的规模最大的投资庞氏骗局，甚至比我们现在看到的类似的

sentences.en: scheme we're seeing right now, but apparently by a cryptocurrency dealer, Sam Bankman-Fried.
sentences.zh: 由加密货币交易商萨姆·班克曼-弗里德（Sam Bankman-Fried）策划的骗局还要大。

sentences.en: These types of frauds where you rob Peter to pay Paul, as they say, are arguably a form of lying.
sentences.zh: 正如人们所说，这种拆东墙补西墙的诈骗可以说是一种谎言。

sentences.en: Would you view people who perpetrate these types of frauds as pathological liars, even
sentences.zh: 你是否会将实施这类诈骗的人视为病理性说谎者，尽管

sentences.en: though, at least in these cases, these individuals appeared to be honest in other areas of their lives?
sentences.zh: 至少在这些案例中，这些人在生活其他领域似乎表现得很诚实？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think if we're going to talk about whether they're pathological liars or not, I'll invite
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为如果我们要在他们是否是病理性说谎者这一点上进行讨论，我会把

sentences.en: your attention back to the way that we've been characterizing pathological lying in our book and the way we characterize it is these are people who prolifically lie, but the lying
sentences.zh: 大家的注意力引回到我们在书中对病理性说谎的表征方式上，我们将其表征为：这些人频繁说谎，但这种说谎

sentences.en: causes distress and dysfunction in their lives and so forth.
sentences.zh: 给他们的生活带来了痛苦和功能失调，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And so when we look at people like Bernie Madoff and other scammers and fraudsters, yeah, I
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们看待像伯尼·麦道夫和其他骗子时，是的，

sentences.en: think it's probably in many cases we're looking at something more along the lines of an antisocial
sentences.zh: 我认为在很多情况下，我们看到的情况更接近于反社会

sentences.en: personality disorder rather than what Drew and I would conceptualize as pathological liars.
sentences.zh: 人格障碍，而不是德鲁（Drew）和我所概念化的病理性说谎者。

sentences.en: So these are people who are certainly doing a lot of lying, but their lying is very specific
sentences.zh: 所以这些人确实在大量说谎，但他们说谎非常具体，

sentences.en: with this malicious intent to manipulate and take advantage of others with this callous disregard, lack of remorse and so forth.
sentences.zh: 带有操纵和占他人便宜的恶意意图，并伴有冷酷的漠视、缺乏悔意等等。

sentences.en: Does pathological lying tend to be a separate disorder or is it associated with other disorders that have, say, a more formal recognized diagnosis at this point?
sentences.zh: 病理性说谎往往是一种独立的障碍，还是与那些目前拥有更正式认可诊断的其他障碍有关？

sentences.en: Well, that's, you know, that's a great question that many times comes with some clinicians.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，这是一个很好的问题，临床医生经常会遇到。

sentences.en: One of the studies Chris and I did was looking specifically at psychotherapists, looking at licensed psychologists.
sentences.zh: 克里斯和我做过的一项研究专门针对心理治疗师，也就是持牌心理学家。

sentences.en: And, you know, when there is no diagnostic label, what do you do?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，当没有诊断标签时，你该怎么办？

sentences.en: So we found a number of our research participants who are licensed psychologists indicated they
sentences.zh: 因此我们发现，我们的一些作为持牌心理学家的研究参与者表示，他们

sentences.en: had come across individuals who are pathological liars and they believed them to be pathological liars.
sentences.zh: 确实遇到过病理性说谎者，并且他们认为这些人就是病理性说谎者。

sentences.en: And so what they ended up doing was to provide some treatment, needed some diagnostic category.
sentences.zh: 所以他们最终的做法是，为了提供一些治疗，需要一个诊断类别。

sentences.en: Many times they would give a personality disorder diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，他们会给出人格障碍的诊断。

sentences.en: And so that happens.
sentences.zh: 所以这种情况确实会发生。

sentences.en: And sometimes, you know, there may be rebuttals or arguments against some of the work Chris
sentences.zh: 而且有时，你知道的，可能会有人对克里斯和我

sentences.en: and I are doing from others saying, well, that pathological lying is just a symptom of something else like a personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 正在做的一些工作提出反驳或争论，他们说，病理性说谎只是某种其他东西（比如人格障碍）的一个症状。

sentences.en: It's a symptom of antisocial personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 它是反社会人格障碍的一种症状。

sentences.en: Some of the work that we've done in our lab assessing individuals, giving them psychological
sentences.zh: 我们在实验室里对个人进行评估、给他们做心理

sentences.en: evaluations, we find that the pathological lying sample, they don't fit the diagnostic criteria for antisocial personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 评估的一些工作表明，病理性说谎样本并不符合反社会人格障碍的诊断标准。

sentences.en: Many of them haven't had any kind of run-ins with the law or any kind of forensic complications.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人没有任何违法乱纪的经历，也没有任何法医学方面的并发症。

sentences.en: Many times there's lack of, there's no aggression.
sentences.zh: 很多时候缺乏攻击性，没有攻击行为。

sentences.en: So aggression is another criteria of antisocial personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 所以攻击性是反社会人格障碍的另一个标准。

sentences.en: Many times, as I said earlier, they tend to feel remorse.
sentences.zh: 就像我刚才说的，很多时候他们往往会感到懊悔。

sentences.en: And so that doesn't fit the same picture as antisocial personality disorder or psychopathy.
sentences.zh: 所以这与反社会人格障碍或精神病态的画像并不吻合。

sentences.en: And so separating that is very important for clinicians.
sentences.zh: 因此，将这一点区分开来对临床医生非常重要。

sentences.en: It's also good for people to understand who might be suffering from pathological lying where they line up.
sentences.zh: 对于可能正在遭受病理性说谎困扰、想要了解自己处于什么位置的人来说，这也是有益的。

sentences.en: And then Charles D.K.
sentences.zh: 然后来自耶鲁大学的查尔斯·D·K（Charles D.K.）

sentences.en: from Yale suggested pathological lying as well being considered for the DSM as a diagnostic entity.
sentences.zh: 也建议将病理性说谎作为一个诊断实体纳入《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》（DSM）中考虑。

sentences.en: And under that specifiers of factitious disorder.
sentences.zh: 并在其下设立人为障碍（factitious disorder）的说明符。

sentences.en: And so Chris and I, based on our research, would agree with Charles D.K.
sentences.zh: 所以克里斯和我在我们的研究基础上，会赞同查尔斯·D·K

sentences.en: suggesting pathological lying being the overarching diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 的建议，即把病理性说谎作为总体诊断。

sentences.en: And then subtypes and specifiers like factitious disorder or pseudologia fantastica.
sentences.zh: 然后是诸如人为障碍或离奇谎言症（pseudologia fantastica）之类的亚型和说明符。

sentences.en: Are there effective treatments for pathological lying?
sentences.zh: 病理性说谎有有效的治疗方法吗？

sentences.en: Can people get better with therapy if they're motivated to do so?
sentences.zh: 如果患者有治疗的动力，他们能通过治疗好转吗？

sentences.en: And if so, what types of therapy work?
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，什么类型的治疗有效？

sentences.en: Well, as a clinician, I tend to hold an optimistic view of change for people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，作为一名临床医生，我对人们的改变往往抱持乐观的看法。

sentences.en: And so that's where I land.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的立场。

sentences.en: You know, we run in the same problem with, you know, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们遇到了同样的问题，也就是——这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: Can people get better?
sentences.zh: 人们能好转吗？

sentences.en: And so we go back to the same problem when we don't have a formal diagnosis for pathological lying.
sentences.zh: 所以我们又回到了同样的问题：当我们对病理性说谎没有正式诊断时，

sentences.en: We don't have research-based treatments to see what is most effective and will these things be helpful.
sentences.zh: 我们就没有基于研究的治疗方法来观察什么最有效以及这些方法是否有帮助。

sentences.en: So that poses a problem for us.
sentences.zh: 所以这给我们带来了问题。

sentences.en: But in our book, we talk about some research we did with therapists and then our own inferences of treatments.
sentences.zh: 但在我们的书中，我们讨论了我们与治疗师合作开展的一些研究，以及我们对治疗方法的推论。

sentences.en: And largely therapists and ourselves, we think that cognitive behavioral therapy would be highly effective to treat and work with people who suffer from pathological lying.
sentences.zh: 大体上，治疗师和我们自己都认为，认知行为疗法对于治疗和帮助那些遭受病理性说谎困扰的人将非常有效。

sentences.en: And so essentially what you can do is help people become aware of their cognitions.
sentences.zh: 因此，你基本上可以做的是帮助人们意识到他们的认知。

sentences.en: What's the function of their lies?
sentences.zh: 他们谎言的功能是什么？

sentences.en: When, which situations might they have a higher proclivity to tell lies?
sentences.zh: 在哪些情况下，他们更有可能说谎？

sentences.en: And typically that's going to be relationally.
sentences.zh: 通常那会是人际关系方面的。

sentences.en: So being aware of those situations.
sentences.zh: 所以要意识到这些情况。

sentences.en: And then a lot of behavioral treatments.
sentences.zh: 然后还有很多行为治疗方法。

sentences.en: So some of these we call differential reinforcement of other behavior or habit reversal training.
sentences.zh: 其中一些我们称之为其他行为的差异强化（differential reinforcement）或习惯逆转训练。

sentences.en: Essentially the idea is you become aware of your behaviors, become aware of when you lie, and not give that attention.
sentences.zh: 本质上的想法是，你要意识到自己的行为，意识到自己什么时候在撒谎，并且不要给予这种行为关注。

sentences.en: Rather reinforce honesty behaviors.
sentences.zh: 而是要去强化诚实的行为。

sentences.en: And that may mean even when honesty doesn't necessarily lead to a good consequence.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，即使诚实并不一定能带来好的结果时，也要这样做。

sentences.en: You know, if you tell someone that asks you, do you like my new haircut?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果有人问你：你喜欢我的新发型吗？

sentences.en: My son just got a new haircut and he doesn't like it too well.
sentences.zh: 我儿子刚剪了个新发型，他自己其实不太喜欢。

sentences.en: So if you get asked that, you know, you could lie to make someone feel good.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你被问到这个问题，你知道的，你可能会为了让别人感觉好一点而撒谎。

sentences.en: Oh, it looks great.
sentences.zh: 哦，看起来好极了。

sentences.en: Or you could be honest and, you know, there's some consequences there.
sentences.zh: 或者你也可以选择说实话，然后，你知道的，这会带来一些后果。

sentences.en: But even with pathological lying, we'd have to reinforce telling the truth, even if the consequence may not be the most desirable for the person.
sentences.zh: 但即使面对病理性说谎，我们也必须强化说实话的行为，即便对当事人来说，其结果可能并非最理想的。

sentences.en: But isn't there kind of a catch-22, though, for the therapist?
sentences.zh: 但对治疗师来说，这难道不是陷入了一种悖论（catch-22）吗？

sentences.en: Because you're dealing with somebody whose problem is lying.
sentences.zh: 因为你在和一个问题就是说谎的人打交道。

sentences.en: So how do you know that your patient is telling you the truth?
sentences.zh: 所以你怎么知道你的患者对你说的就是实话呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And that kind of fueled a lot of Chris and I, our interest in this early on, in our work early on, in just deception within therapy.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上激发了克里斯和我早期对这个课题的兴趣，在我们早期的工作中，仅仅是关于治疗中的欺骗行为。

sentences.en: So therapy rests on the assumption of honesty.
sentences.zh: 因此，心理治疗是建立在诚实这一假设之上的。

sentences.en: That all that we do in talk therapy is that we assume our patients are honeSt.
sentences.zh: 我们在谈话疗法中所做的一切，都是假设我们的患者是诚实的。

sentences.en: One of the things with pathological lying to understand is, even though they tell lies much more frequently than most people, they're not lying all the time about everything.
sentences.zh: 关于病理性说谎需要理解的一点是，尽管他们比大多数人更频繁地撒谎，但他们并不是对所有事情都在无时无刻地撒谎。

sentences.en: And so even in some of our assessment studies, the question I would ask people at the end is, what have you lied to me today about?
sentences.zh: 因此，甚至在我们的一些评估研究中，我最后会问参与者的问题是：你今天对我撒谎了什么？

sentences.en: And many of them would indicate nothing.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人会回答：没有。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: You know, why haven't you lied?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你为什么没撒谎？

sentences.en: And many of them would say answers like, well, this is a real struggle from me.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人会回答这样的话：嗯，这对我来说真的是个巨大的挣扎。

sentences.en: I'm hoping to advance science.
sentences.zh: 我希望推动科学的发展。

sentences.en: If you learn from me, you can help out other people.
sentences.zh: 如果你能从我身上学到东西，你就能帮助其他人。

sentences.en: So they're not lying all the time about everything.
sentences.zh: 所以他们并不是对所有事情都在无时无刻地撒谎。

sentences.en: And I think that's important to note.
sentences.zh: 我认为这一点值得注意。

sentences.en: The other thing to note there, too, is I think very important for therapists is when someone lies to us, we typically take it personal and get defensive.
sentences.zh: 那里还有一点需要注意，我认为对治疗师来说非常重要，那就是当有人对我们撒谎时，我们通常会把它当作针对个人的事情并产生防备心理。

sentences.en: And that typically isn't productive in therapy.
sentences.zh: 而这在治疗中通常是没有成效的。

sentences.en: So the way you overcome that is kind of know your stance, become non-defensive, and use that to try to understand with the patient, you know, what's the function of this lie?
sentences.zh: 所以克服这一点的办法是明确自己的立场，保持无防备状态，并以此去尝试与患者一同理解：这个谎言的功能是什么？

sentences.en: Are you wanting me to give you praise?
sentences.zh: 你是想让我夸奖你吗？

sentences.en: Are you wanting me to think of you in a certain light?
sentences.zh: 你是想让我以某种特定的眼光看待你吗？

sentences.en: Are you trying to form a certain impression?
sentences.zh: 你是想树立某种印象吗？

sentences.en: Do you not want me to think poorly of you?
sentences.zh: 你是不希望我对你有不好的看法吗？

sentences.en: But if you start asking those questions, I think that that would breed more trust and compassion for the person to lean in and understand them.
sentences.zh: 但如果你开始提出这些问题，我认为这会为对方孕育出更多的信任和同理心，让他们能够倾心并理解他们。

sentences.en: And that's why Chris and I really, you know, wrote the book we wrote was to lean in and understand pathological lying much deeper rather than just, you know,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么克里斯和真正我，你知道的，写了我们那本书，是为了深入倾听和理解病理性说谎，而不是仅仅，你知道的，

sentences.en: turning away and saying, you know, these are crazies that we can never understand.
sentences.zh: 转身走开，然后说，你知道的，这些是疯子，我们永远无法理解。

sentences.en: But, you know, people who are suffering and want help.
sentences.zh: 而是，你知道的，他们是痛苦并需要帮助的人。

sentences.en: What about group therapy as a treatment?
sentences.zh: 那么把集体治疗作为一种治疗手段呢？

sentences.en: Doesn't that give you the option, the opportunity for other people to sort of call out liars as opposed to having the therapist have to do that?
sentences.zh: 这难道不会给你提供一种选择和机会，让其他人来指出说谎者的问题，而不必由治疗师来做这件事吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: We suggest group therapy.
sentences.zh: 我们建议进行集体治疗。

sentences.en: And I'm laughing because you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我笑是因为你完全说对了。

sentences.en: You know, one of the ways that group therapy works is the therapist doesn't have to call out the patient.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，集体治疗起作用的方式之一就是治疗师不必去当面指出患者的问题。

sentences.en: So the brilliance of any kind of interpersonal work is other members in the group can say, hey, you know, BS, you just lied.
sentences.zh: 任何群际工作（interpersonal work）的精妙之处都在于，小组中的其他成员可以说，嘿，你知道吗，少废话，你刚才撒谎了。

sentences.en: And that works so much, so well in a group therapy context because it's not about patient-client opposing each other.
sentences.zh: 这在集体治疗的语境下效果非常好，因为这不涉及患者与临床医生的对立。

sentences.en: Rather, it's about other people are seeing this thing in you too.
sentences.zh: 相反，这是关于其他人也在你身上看到了这一点。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Hart, let me throw this one at you.
sentences.zh: 好吧，哈特博士（Dr. Hart），让我抛出这个问题考考你。

sentences.en: How can people recognize and protect themselves from pathological liars?
sentences.zh: 人们该如何识别病理性说谎者并保护自己免受其害？

sentences.en: Are there telltale signs or particular personality traits of the most hardened pathological liars?
sentences.zh: 对于那些最顽固的病理性说谎者，是否存在明显的征兆或特定的人格特质？

sentences.en: I think we know that we're very bad at telling when people are lying to us.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都知道，我们在分辨别人是否在对我们撒谎这方面非常糟糕。

sentences.en: And pathological liars, I mean, how do we suss them out as opposed to just an everyday liar?
sentences.zh: 而对于病理性说谎者，我的意思是，除了日常的说谎者之外，我们该如何把他们筛查出来？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a perplexing problem.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个令人困惑的难题。

sentences.en: And you're correct.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: People are really poor lie detectors.
sentences.zh: 人们其实很不擅长识破谎言。

sentences.en: If we look at people's ability to detect when people are lying versus being honest in laboratory studies, what we find is that people perform at only slightly above chance levels.
sentences.zh: 如果我们看一下实验室研究中人们辨别谎言与实话的能力，我们会发现人们的正确率仅略高于瞎猜的水平。

sentences.en: That is, they'd be almost as effective just flipping a coin, guessing whether someone's being honest or not.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，他们去猜某人是否说实话，效果几乎和抛硬币差不多。

sentences.en: And it really kind of gets back to the fact that we are a cooperative species.
sentences.zh: 这其实归结于这样一个事实：我们是一个合作物种。

sentences.en: And so we tend to have what's referred to as a truth-the-fault.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们往往倾向于存在所谓的“信任默认”。

sentences.en: That is, we just assume people are being honest when they speak.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我们在别人说话时，只会默认他们说的是实话。

sentences.en: And so we tend not to be on guard for deception.
sentences.zh: 所以我们往往不会对欺骗保持警惕。

sentences.en: So when we look at how people actually detect lying, it's not by, you know, seeing that someone's looking askance or they're, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们观察人们实际上是如何识破谎言的时，并不是通过观察某人眼神闪烁，或者他们

sentences.en: fidgeting with their hands or shuffling their feet.
sentences.zh: 手部局促不安，或是脚下挪动。

sentences.en: But rather, we detect people are lying by hearing them say things that conflict with factual information we actually know.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们是通过听到他们说的话与我们实际已知的事实相矛盾，来识破谎言的。

sentences.en: Or we find out they're lying by gathering additional information from third parties.
sentences.zh: 或者我们通过从第三方收集更多信息，发现他们在说谎。

sentences.en: Or in some cases, people just feel guilty and confess.
sentences.zh: 或者在某些情况下，人们只是感到内疚并坦白了。

sentences.en: And so when we look at how could we avoid being duped by pathological liars, my answer would be it's the same way we avoid being duped by everyone else.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们探讨如何避免被病理性说谎者欺骗时，我的回答是，这和我们避免被其他人欺骗的方法是一样的。

sentences.en: And primarily what that is, is we have, we are sensitive to signs of trustworthiness.
sentences.zh: 最主要的是，我们对是否值得信任的信号很敏感。

sentences.en: When we meet people, we walk in with usually a fairly trusting attitude, but we only trust people so far.
sentences.zh: 当我们遇到他人时，通常会带着相当信任的态度走进去，但我们对人的信任也是有限度的。

sentences.en: And so, for example, if we know that someone has an incentive to lie to us, an incentive to manipulate us, we're going to be more on guard and more apt to detect their dishonesty.
sentences.zh: 因此，举个例子，如果我们知道某人有向我们说谎的动机，有操纵我们的动机，我们就会提高警惕，更容易察觉他们的不诚实。

sentences.en: Likewise, if we can rely on people's reputations, if I know nothing about your reputation,
sentences.zh: 同样，如果我们能依赖人们的声誉，如果我对你的声誉一无所知，

sentences.en: I'm going to be a little bit more suspicious of things you say than if I know you quite well and know you to have a reputation as being an honest person.
sentences.zh: 比起我相当了解你并知道你是个诚实的人来说，我对你所说的话会更加怀疑。

sentences.en: But generally, when we've talked to people about pathological liars that they have met or known and how they knew those people were lying,
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，当我们与人们谈论他们遇到或认识的病理性说谎者以及他们是如何知道这些人说谎的时，

sentences.en: what we find is they say that the people say unbelievable things.
sentences.zh: 我们发现他们说这些人会说出令人难以置信的话。

sentences.en: That is, they're making claims that just don't seem likely to have actually happened.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，他们提出的说辞看起来根本不可能真正发生过。

sentences.en: Or they say things that are inconsistent.
sentences.zh: 或者他们说的话前后矛盾。

sentences.en: And so, for example, you were mentioning the case of George Santos.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，你刚才提到了乔治·桑托斯的例子。

sentences.en: I believe he indicated his mother died during the 9-11 attacks and then later claimed that she had died a decade later.
sentences.zh: 我记得他曾暗示他的母亲在911袭击中丧生，后来又声称她是在十年后去世的。

sentences.en: And so, when we see inconsistency in information, that can be a cue.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们看到信息不一致时，这可能就是一个线索。

sentences.en: So, really what we're doing is we're looking for coherence, we're looking for proof, and we're looking for the reputational status of a person.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们实际上在做的是寻找连贯性、寻找证据，并考察一个人的声誉地位。

sentences.en: All of those together can inform us of who we should be suspicious of and maybe who we can be more trusting of.
sentences.zh: 所有这些加在一起，可以告诉我们应该对谁保持警惕，也许对谁可以更加信任。

sentences.en: So, how will your upcoming book online differ from the one that we at APA have already published?
sentences.zh: 那么，你们即将出版的在线新书与我们APA已经出版的那本有什么不同呢？

sentences.en: I found that to be quite accessible.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那本很容易读懂。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't think you need to be a psychologist to read that, but what's going to be in your new book?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得不需要成为心理学家也能读懂，但你们的新书里会有什么内容呢？

sentences.en: Well, thanks for the kind words about the first book.
sentences.zh: 嗯，谢谢你对第一本书的美言。

sentences.en: We were hoping to make it accessible, but the difference in the second book is it doesn't focus on pathological liars.
sentences.zh: 我们当时希望这本书通俗易懂，但第二本书的不同之处在于它不以病理性说谎者为重点。

sentences.en: We certainly address pathological liars, but we look at people who lie prolifically or tell extremely consequential lies aside from pathological liars.
sentences.zh: 我们当然会讨论病理性说谎者，但除了病理性说谎者之外，我们还会关注那些惯于说谎或说极其重大谎言的人。

sentences.en: So, you know, we're probably talking in a lot of cases about people who exhibit signs of psychopathy or antisocial personality disorder or other personality disorders.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，在很多情况下，我们可能是在谈论那些表现出精神病态、反社会人格障碍或其他人格障碍迹象的人。

sentences.en: But really what we're interested in is the people who tell the consequential lies or the extremely frequent lies where they develop a reputation as being a dishonest person.
sentences.zh: 但我们真正感兴趣的是那些说重大谎言或极其频繁说谎的人，他们因此建立起了不诚实者的声誉。

sentences.en: And we're looking at how do they develop into these types of big liars?
sentences.zh: 我们在研究他们是如何演变成这类“大话精”的？

sentences.en: What are the consequences of their big lying, both on themselves, on the people around them, and on society more broadly?
sentences.zh: 他们的大谎言会带来什么后果，无论是对自己、对身边的人，还是对更广泛的社会？

sentences.en: And then we examine ways for cultivating honesty, both in ourselves and the people around us.
sentences.zh: 然后，我们探讨了培养诚实的方法，既包括我们自己，也包括我们身边的人。

sentences.en: And we talk to a certain degree about different tactics we can use to avoid being duped.
sentences.zh: 我们在某种程度上讨论了我们可以用来避免受骗的不同策略。

sentences.en: So what are you both working on now?
sentences.zh: 那么你们俩现在都在忙些什么？

sentences.en: What are the big questions that you're trying to answer at the moment?
sentences.zh: 你们目前试图解答的重大问题是什么？

sentences.en: One of the things I kind of mentioned earlier that Chris and I with Victoria Tower are working on, digging deeper into the etiology.
sentences.zh: 我刚才顺便提到了一点，我和克里斯以及维多利亚·托ower正在深入研究病因学。

sentences.en: So onset and cause of pathological lying, you know, the big broad question all psychologists have, nature, nurture, how much of one or the other.
sentences.zh: 也就是病理性说谎的发作和起因，你知道的，所有心理学家都有的那个宏大而广泛的问题：先天还是后天，各自占多少比例。

sentences.en: And as a clinician, most clinicians want to understand etiology.
sentences.zh: 作为临床医生，大多数临床医生都想了解病因学。

sentences.en: So we're really digging into those questions that we don't know about how it develops and how it maintains.
sentences.zh: 所以我们真的在深入研究那些我们尚不了解的问题，即它是如何发展和维持的。

sentences.en: And then are there certain developmental trajectories that lead to a path of pathological lying compared to normative lying?
sentences.zh: 那么，与正常说谎相比，是否存在某些导致走向病理性说谎的发展轨迹？

sentences.en: So that's where we're focusing a little more specifically right now with some of our research.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们目前通过部分研究将重点放得更具体一点的地方。

sentences.en: Chris, does you want to add to that?
sentences.zh: 克里斯，你想补充一下吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, we're also doing a little bit of work on the motivators, what drives people to lie, especially what drives people to lie to excess.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们还在做一些关于动机的工作，是什么驱使人们说谎，尤其是是什么驱使人们过度说谎。

sentences.en: And so we can see that people don't lie randomly.
sentences.zh: 因此我们可以看到人们并不是随机说谎的。

sentences.en: They don't lie for no reason at all.
sentences.zh: 他们不会无缘无故地撒谎。

sentences.en: If we see someone lying, there's some sort of an incentive that's driving them to lie.
sentences.zh: 如果我们看到有人在说谎，背后必然有某种动机在驱使他们说谎。

sentences.en: But we also, most people balance that with some disincentives to lie.
sentences.zh: 但我们大多数人也会将此与一些不说谎的消极动机进行权衡。

sentences.en: So, you know, if you are caught lying, it's certainly going to affect you reputationally,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果你被抓到说谎，这肯定会影响你的声誉，

sentences.en: which is going to hamper your ability to have the types of social relationships you desire.
sentences.zh: 这会阻碍你建立自己期望的社会关系的能力。

sentences.en: But then we also each have a moral sense of self that seems to curb most of our bad behavior.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我们每个人都有道德自我意识，这似乎能够遏制我们的大部分不良行为。

sentences.en: So we don't refrain from bad behavior simply because we're worried about getting caught.
sentences.zh: 所以我们克制不良行为不仅仅是因为担心被抓。

sentences.en: We refrain from it because we don't want to view ourselves as being awful people.
sentences.zh: 我们克制是因为我们不想把自己视为糟糕的人。

sentences.en: And so trying to understand those complex motivations that are behind people's decisions to lie, especially lie prolifically, or remain honest is another area of interest of ours.
sentences.zh: 因此，试图理解人们决定说谎（尤其是频繁说谎）或保持诚实背后的复杂动机，是我们感兴趣的另一个领域。

sentences.en: And then one other thing more recently, Chris has led, is developing an instrument to assess pathological lying more fully.
sentences.zh: 最近还有一件事，由克里斯主导，就是开发一个更全面评估病理性说谎的工具。

sentences.en: An instrument that researchers and clinicians can use so we can assess pathological lying to answer, you know, some of these questions,
sentences.zh: 一个研究人员和临床医生可以使用的工具，以便我们能够评估病理性说谎，从而回答其中一些问题，

sentences.en: get a little more accurate prevalence rate and study these things.
sentences.zh: 获得更准确的患病率并研究这些事情。

sentences.en: Well, I want to thank you both for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我要感谢你们今天能来参加。

sentences.en: I have found our conversation really interesting and enlightening.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们的对话非常有趣且富有启发性。

sentences.en: And I mean that honestly.
sentences.zh: 我是真心这么觉得的。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 不客气，这是我们的荣幸。

sentences.en: We enjoyed it as well, honestly.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我们也聊得很开心。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having us.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我们做客。

sentences.en: It's been a great pleasure talking with you.
sentences.zh: 和您交谈非常愉快。

sentences.en: You can find a link to pre-order the book, Big Liars, on APA's website, www.apa.org, and just go there and search for Big Liars.
sentences.zh: 您可以在APA的网站www.apa.org上找到预订新书《大话精》的链接，只需访问该网站并搜索“Big Liars”。

sentences.en: Or if you can't wait, you can order their current book, Pathological Lying Theory, Research and Practice, also on the APA website.
sentences.zh: 或者如果您等不及了，您也可以在APA网站上订购他们目前出版的书籍《病理性说谎：理论、研究与实践》。

sentences.en: For previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology, visit us at speakingofpsychology.org, or you can find us on Apple, Stitcher, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 有关《心理学演讲》往期节目的内容，请访问我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org，或者您也可以在 Apple、Stitcher 或任何您获取播客的地方找到我们。

sentences.en: And if you like what you heard, please leave us a review.
sentences.zh: 如果您喜欢我们的话，请给我们留个评论。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at APA.org.
sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，可以通过电子邮件 speakingofpsychology@APA.org 联系我们。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学演讲》由李·韦纳曼制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Kondayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的音频剪辑师是克里斯·孔达扬。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 谢谢收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯，代表美国心理学协会向您问候。
